targets.name: Moon's south pole (Artemis III regions)
targets.anchor_note: The nine regions are anchored on the USGS positions of the features they are named after (NASA publishes no centre points), so this target is placed at the pole and stands for all nine.

slope_median_deg.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
slope_median_deg.note: Each region's value is the median slope over the 10 km window. 10 km window at the anchor, polar stereographic 240 m grid, slopes at 240 m.

slope_p90_deg.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
slope_p90_deg.note: Each region's value is the 90th percentile slope over the 10 km window. 10 km window at the anchor, polar stereographic 240 m grid, slopes at 240 m.

share_under_10.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
share_under_10.note: Each region's value is the share of the 10 km window with slope under 10°. 10 km window at the anchor, polar stereographic 240 m grid, slopes at 240 m.

share_under_5.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
share_under_5.note: Each region's value is the share of the 10 km window with slope under 5°. 10 km window at the anchor, polar stereographic 240 m grid, slopes at 240 m.

relief_m.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
relief_m.note: Each region's value is the 5th to 95th percentile height range over the 10 km window. 10 km window at the anchor, polar stereographic 240 m grid, slopes at 240 m.

t_min_k.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
t_min_k.note: Each region's value is the median over the 10 km window of the winter-minimum map. Median over the 10 km window of the winter minimum surface temperature (polar_south_80_winter_min-float.tif).

t_min_coldest_k.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
t_min_coldest_k.note: Each region's value is the coldest pixel of the winter-minimum map in the 10 km window. Coldest pixel in the 10 km window. Below about 25 K, the coldest ground temperature the Diviner team reports for the south pole (https://www.diviner.ucla.edu/science); readings this low are at the limit of what the instrument can measure, so read it as 'colder than about 25 K'.

t_max_k.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
t_max_k.note: Each region's value is the median over the 10 km window of the summer-maximum map. Median over the 10 km window of the summer maximum surface temperature (polar_south_80_summer_max-float.tif).

t_swing_k.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
t_swing_k.note: Each region's value is the median of the summer-maximum map minus median of the winter-minimum map, 10 km window. Summer-to-winter range of surface temperature, not a day-to-night swing.

frozen_months.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
frozen_months.note: Each region's value is the coolest pixel of the summer-maximum map in the 10 km window. The window's coolest spot peaks at 133 K in summer, below 273 K, so it stays frozen all year.

lit_share.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
lit_share.note: Each region's value is the best-lit pixel in the 10 km window. Best-lit 120 m pixel in the 10 km window, as a fraction of time (0–1), at the surface.

lit_share_median.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
lit_share_median.note: Each region's value is the median over the 10 km window. Median over the 10 km window, fraction of time (0–1).

psr_share.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
psr_share.note: Each region's value is the share of 120 m pixels in the 10 km window flagged as permanent shadow. Pixel value +20000 means permanent shadow and -20000 means not; the meaning comes from the product label on the LOLA team's node (http://imbrium.mit.edu/EXTRAS/ILLUMINATION/IMG/LPSR_75S_120M_201608.LBL). File: https://pgda.gsfc.nasa.gov/data/MoonIllumination/LPSR_75S_120M_201608.TIF

noon_sun_deg.stat: median of NASA's nine Artemis III candidate regions (10 km window each)
noon_sun_deg.note: Each region's value is the 90 − |latitude|. Mean sun height at the anchor; the Moon's 1.54° tilt moves it about ±1.5° over the year.

thermal_inertia_moon_wide.note: Moon-wide average at 273 K, 55 +/- 2; not mapped at the pole (the Diviner map stops at 70 degrees latitude)

dci.stat: median of the 3×3 pixels at the site

ground_strength_note.stat: median TES thermal inertia against NASA's 100–140 landing-site rule

frozen_months.stat: months with mean ground temperature below 0 C
frozen_months.note: NASA's Mars fact sheet gives an average temperature of about 214 K (−59 C) and a daily range of 184–242 K at the Viking 1 site, all below 273 K (0 C). This value rests on that planet-wide average and this site's published night minimum (-93 C ground), not on a month-by-month record at the site; mid-latitude summers can be warmer than the planet average.

daily_swing_c.stat: twice the published half-amplitude of the daily air-temperature cycle
daily_swing_c.note: Twice the published 26 K half-amplitude of the daily air-temperature cycle (first 250 sols).

t_min_air_c.note: No single coldest air temperature is stated in the text; not read off figures.

t_min_ground_c.stat: night-time minimum of the regolith over one Mars year
t_min_ground_c.note: Night-time minimum of the regolith on the crater floor, 'about 180 K' in the text (−93 °C); frost is briefly stable when the ground is below 185 K.

daily_ground_swing_c.note: The text gives the night minimum (about 180 K) but no daily ground maximum or swing; not read off figures.

dust_tau.stat: visible column optical depth just after a January 2022 local storm
dust_tau.note: Visible column optical depth (Mastcam-Z 880 nm channel; dust plus some ice) near 0.4 just after a January 2022 local storm (Ls ~156°, northern late summer) and near 0.3 before it, close to the seasonal minimum. The same paper says the 9 µm dust optical depth is about half the visible value; we did not convert anything. Dusty-season values are higher (the storm peaked near 2).

noon_sun_deg.note: Mean noon sun height; Mars's 25.2° tilt moves it up to ±25° over the year.
